item.title: Questions about the fine details
item.content:encoded:
Hello. I've been forced out of lurking by my interest for Resurrection canon, and I have questions to those in the know.

I sincerely apologize in advance.
No, I really do. That is a lot of questions.

1. What would the current containment procedures for Iris look like? Ones outlined in the article wouldn't fit an MTF officer, and she was given a Level 4 clearance in one of the tales. What would she be allowed to do? What material benefits would she be allowed access to? How freely can she move around?

2. How does Tav-666 operate in regards to Alpha-9? What are the actual things they do day-to-day? What are their specific duties? What exactly do they report, and to who?

3. Has Iris ever met Clef? Does she know Clef's assigned to watch Alpha-9? What does she know about Clef?

4. How much does Iris know about Foundation, and the anomalous world in general?

5. How old, approximately, would Atkus be?

6. This one might be spoilery. Were Andrews and Beatrice friends with Iris in a world post-Incident Zero? Or are her memories of them simply remnants of a reality that no longer exists?

7. This one is very loaded. Why does Iris display no psychological trauma from her containment and all events that preceded it? Going by her characterization in the canon, she appears to be perfectly well-adjusted to her circumstances, and her interactions with the outside world in Girls' Night Out (and Foundation personnel in general) appear to be extremely uncharacteristic of someone in her circumstances. She is never explicitly hostile to the organization that made her suffer so much, and the only mention of her possible mental health issues is a single line in a tale that doesn't even feature her.

8. In Harm's Way involves a meeting of Foundation senior staff concerning Alpha-9, which is a lot of people - Moose, Bright, Gillespie, Atkus etc. etc. What is their role regarding Alpha-9? What do they do in a strictly bureaucratic sense?

9. What do Crow and Mann do for Alpha-9? Also in a strictly bureaucratic sense.

10. On what basis are grunt agents like Zhang and Johnson recruited into Alpha-9?

11. On occasion that being a completely new user or asking a shitton of questions as introduction isn't a major turn-off, how can I contribute to the canon?

item.content:encoded:
Hey, this is just me spitballing here for a probable base for MTF Alpha-Niner Last Hope.
I haven't done much reading with the Omega 7 story arc, but I have read the whole of Resurrection story list.

Heli-carrier. Again, this is not some Marvel fanboy input, the problem I see with the MTF Last hope is tied to the saying, "Putting All your Eggs in one Basket." If they set up shop at any of the sites, they risk the problem of putting the site as a target by the other relevant organizations, such as what happen with Girls Night Out.

This brings me back to the Heli-carrier but again. If it is large enough, (And I'm basing this on the scale the Heli-carrier in the MCU in Avengers) and more overall design right you can essentially have a mobile containment site. They can of course be temporary for when the item recovered during a raid or something similar like the the SCP-008 outbreak that 105 help sort out. Or even keep 'useful' SCP on the Heli-carrier for the MTF to use in particular situation.

Again, you will end up 'putting all your eggs in one basket' but at least it mobile. You can even call the ship 'The Sword of Damocles' to reflect the important of what the Heli-carrier and its mission objective.

item.title: Can't believe this canon manage to lay under my radar for so long
item.content:encoded:
It seems quite polarizing based on the discussion pages, some people can't seem to stand this thing, but others welcome it as an addition to the website's canons.

Personally, I am one of the latter. I find this canon quiet nostalgic to when I first found this website years ago, and many of these tropes were still common - but it also takes it in it's own direction, one where I don't just see this as "A place where you can get away with the poor writing of Series 1", but rather a reconstruction of that era that takes what the old times were known for, except doing them much better.

And, of course, regardless of how you feel about the canon, I'm glad this stuff has it's own place on the Wiki. It's all for fun, in the end.

item.content:encoded:
For the purposes of Resurrection:

  • There is only one O5-2, O5-4, O5-6, O5-7, O5-8, O5-9, O5-10, and O5-13. (At least, unless we decide otherwise.)
  • There are many of O5-1 and O5-11 (or at least, no single person will ever represent themselves as the single O5-1 or O5-11).
  • There may or may not be more than one O5-3, O5-5, and O5-12 (but some personality limitations may apply).
  • Most O5s have many Factotum/assistants, who sometimes act for them, and may sometimes have anomalous abilities of some kind.

If you're looking to write a new Council member character, O5-1 or especially O5-11 would be ideal.

Check out The High Court With The Magic Army for Resurrection, and O5 Command Dossier for many canons. The Dossier also gives more possibilities than I laid out here.

item.content:encoded: I have been reading this canon since it had been started and I would like to say something. This canon is not like the other Foundation stories. It develops very slowly, with all this long dialogues and black-and-white scenes, like in an old good detective movie. But. I've never read a story on this site wich lays out the inner world of the Foundation better than these tales. The immersion is incredibly deep. Every character has their own lifestory, features, family and psychological experience. And most of all, they feel and react in an adequate way, as if they were living people. I would like to thank all the contributors for writing this canon.
